labels_create: The Living Brain service (Rust, Cratefield venture)
Per-person modeling and the learning layer
Owlpost: digests and the brain's inbox
Blocked on a Cratefield harness change

epic.title: Epic 2: The living wiki. Markdown pages with sources that the brain keeps improving
epic.body:
The memory is not a black-box vector store: it is a Markdown wiki the customer can read, edit and export (Karpathy's LLM-wiki pattern: raw sources, compiled pages, an index, and lint passes). The brain writes it from conversations, links every fact to its source, and on a schedule merges, reconciles and refreshes it. A learning layer models each person so answers and briefs improve every week.

**Stack.** A Rust Cargo workspace consumed as a Cratefield venture (`cratefield-core`, `cratefield-runtime-cloudflare`, modules from the harness repo by git until the 0.5 release round, [Cratefield/harness#464](https://github.com/Cratefield/harness/issues/464)), deployed as one Cloudflare Worker with D1, R2, KV and a venture-owned Durable Object, the same shape as `Owlpost-to/backend`. Modules only see ports (`Database`, `TextModel`, `Mailer`, `Realtime`, `Defer`, `Blob`, `KeyValue`, `Signer`, `Payments`); adapters are the only vendor-aware code. Email goes through **Owlpost** (Resend-compatible API, inbound agent inboxes).

**Learning layer and licensing.** Honcho's server is AGPL-3.0; its SDKs are Apache-2.0. Start on the hosted `api.honcho.dev` through the SDK, never embed or modify the server, and rebuild the parts we keep as a Cratefield module before scale.

**Children**
{{harness_embed}} {{pages}} {{extract}} {{citations}} {{search}} {{evolve}} {{learning}} {{crypto}} {{export}}

children.title: Harness: Embeddings and VectorIndex ports (Workers AI + Vectorize, pgvector natively)
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. No dependencies inside the epic.

- `Embedder` port (batch embed text → `Vec<f32>`), adapters: `adapter-workers-ai`, `adapter-openai-compatible`.
- `VectorIndex` port (upsert, delete, query with metadata filter), adapters: Cloudflare Vectorize; pgvector on `runtime-native`.
- Metadata filters must support the scope field so permission filtering happens inside the query.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Parity test: same results shape on Vectorize and pgvector.
- [ ] Scope filter applied in the index query, not after.

children.title: Page store: entities, Markdown, links, history
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. No dependencies inside the epic.

- Page = entity (person, project, decision, customer, system, glossary) with Markdown body in R2 and metadata in D1: slug, type, scope, `[[backlinks]]`, version history.
- Typed frontmatter schema per entity type (as in chi-brain's `schemas/`).
- Human edits are first-class and win over machine edits until reconciled.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every page version is recoverable.
- [ ] A human edit is never silently overwritten by the brain.

children.title: Listen → Write: turn conversations into page updates
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{pages}}.

- Batch new messages per channel (cron + `Defer`), extract facts, decisions, owners, and propose page diffs.
- Each fact keeps its source: Slack permalink, author, timestamp, scope.
- Skip noise (reactions, "thanks", bots).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A decision stated in a thread appears on the right project page with its permalink.
- [ ] Facts from a private channel never land on a shared page.

children.title: Citations everywhere: fact → source, answer → page
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{extract}}.

- Inline citation markers in page Markdown resolve to sources the reader is allowed to see; others render as "restricted source".
- Answers in Slack cite wiki pages, and pages cite messages.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Clicking a citation as a user without access shows no content from it.

children.title: Hybrid search over pages and sources
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{harness_embed}}, {{pages}}.

- Embeddings per page section + full-text (D1 FTS5); rank by both with recency.
- Exposed as a tool to the agent loop and to MCP clients (Epic 3).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Search respects scopes (test with a private-channel fact).
- [ ] p95 latency recorded.

children.title: Evolve: nightly merge, reconcile, refresh (the wiki lints itself)
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{extract}}, {{search}}.

Cron jobs (`Module::scheduled`):
- **Merge** duplicate pages (same entity, different names).
- **Reconcile** contradictions: open a "needs a human" card in Slack with both sources instead of guessing.
- **Refresh** stale facts (age + newer conflicting mention), rewrite summaries, fix broken backlinks.
- A changelog page per night: what the brain changed and why.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every automated change is in the nightly changelog with a reason.
- [ ] Contradictions are surfaced, never silently resolved.

children.title: Learning layer: per-person profiles and what works
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{extract}}.

- Feed messages (and, in Epic 3, agent sessions) to Honcho via the Apache-2.0 SDK against `api.honcho.dev`; store returned peer representations per user and scope.
- Use them to tailor answers and briefs ("prefers small PRs").
- An ADR on replacing Honcho with an in-house Cratefield module (profiles + periodic "dreaming" passes).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Users can view and delete their own profile.
- [ ] No AGPL server code is embedded or modified.

children.title: Per-scope envelope encryption, blind-index search and crypto-shredding
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{pages}}, {{search}}.

Filed directly as #43; see the issue for the full body. One DEK per scope wrapped by a KMS workspace key (customer-managed on Teams), crypto-shredding, HMAC blind indexes for keyword search, per-scope vector namespaces, local decrypt-and-search in the CLI and PWA.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] No plaintext page body or source text at rest in D1 or R2.

children.title: Export and sync: Markdown zip and Obsidian-compatible vault
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{pages}}.

- One-click export of the whole wiki (respecting the exporter's scopes) as an Obsidian vault.
- Optional one-way git sync to a customer repo.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] An export opens in Obsidian with working backlinks.
- [ ] Export contains only what the exporter may see.
